name: Black anarchism
summary: Black anarchism combines opposition to the state, capitalism and hierarchy with a politics of Black self-determination and anti-racism. It seeks a stateless, classless federation of cooperative communes, reached through direct action, community self-defense and rank-and-file organizing, and rejects both vanguard parties and white-dominated anarchism. It also opposes sexism and homophobia, including inside Black nationalist movements.
scope: The Black power-era and later tendency documented in Lorenzo Kom'boa Ervin's Anarchism and the Black Revolution and Ashanti Alston's writings, with roots in Lucy Parsons, Martin Sostre, Kuwasi Balagoon and Ella Baker's anti-leadership organizing. It represents the social-anarchist mainstream of the tendency (anarchist communism and syndicalism with Black autonomous organizing) and excludes Black nationalists who hold state power as their goal and individualist currents.

keyFigures.name: Lorenzo Kom'boa Ervin
keyFigures.role: Author of Anarchism and the Black Revolution and a leading Black anarchist organizer.

keyFigures.name: Ashanti Alston
keyFigures.role: Former Black Panther and Black Liberation Army member turned anarchist writer and speaker.

keyFigures.name: Lucy Parsons
keyFigures.role: Early social anarchist who tied racism to capitalism and urged armed self-defense.

sources.title: Black anarchism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition, key thinkers, structural anti-racism, critique of white anarchism.

sources.title: Anarchism and the Black Revolution
sources.author: Lorenzo Kom'boa Ervin
sources.usedFor: Positions on state, capitalism, property, violence, organization, police and prisons, drugs, religion, patriarchy and economy.

sources.title: Beyond Nationalism, But Not Without It
sources.author: Ashanti Alston
sources.usedFor: Relation to Black nationalism, sexism, homophobia, religious communities, anti-leadership organizing.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Ervin wants services run by communities and the Panther-style survival programs were community-run, so a state-provided scheme is not the adherent's preferred model; this is inferred, not stated.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Adherents aim to abolish the wage system rather than raise its floor, yet would not oppose better pay won by strikes; the sources do not address a legal minimum.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ervin attributes unemployment, rising prices and racial exclusion to capitalist exploitation and advocates common ownership with production for need.

public-ownership.rationale: Ervin wants industry held in common and run by workers' councils, not by the state, which he calls part of the problem; nationalization is therefore not the aim.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Ervin demands reparations paid by government and the rich but seeks to abolish the state and its taxation rather than tune its rates; adherents are not clearly for or against.

unions-good.rationale: Ervin backs rank-and-file controlled, anarcho-syndicalist unions with Black caucuses, while criticizing bureaucratic ones, so unions are good in their democratic form.

property-fundamental.rationale: Ervin's anarchist communism abolishes private and state property and endorses seizing slumlord housing for tenant cooperatives.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents want corporations abolished and industry taken over by workers, and distrust the state as regulator; regulation is at best a stopgap.

cut-welfare.rationale: Ervin demands an end to racism and sexism in relief benefits rather than their removal and wants community institutions funded; the dependency argument is a capitalist one.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ervin describes a classless society with common ownership and production organized by workers' councils and voluntary associations.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Ervin treats police as an occupying force and the state as an enemy of Black liberation, so state surveillance of any justification is rejected; inferred from this stance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Ervin calls dope death, blames state and police for protecting the trade, and calls for community anti-drug programs and rehab clinics rather than legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Ervin prefers direct community action against fascist groups to state laws; the sources do not address speech law, so this is inferred from anti-statism.

strong-leader.rationale: Ervin demands federations without permanent leaders, rotating and recallable delegates, and rejects rule by any party or person in the people's name.

state-harmful.rationale: Ervin states that government will not free Black people and is part of the problem, and Alston calls for power to the people staying with the people, so the state is rejected as such.

limit-guns.rationale: Ervin calls for community self-defense units and a Black peoples' militia and urges learning to make arms if firearms become scarce, so gun restriction is opposed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Ervin writes that the cops are not our friends or allies, calls for disarming and demilitarizing police and eventually replacing them with community self-defense.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Black anarchist sources do not address sex work; adherents' views split between bodily autonomy and anti-exploitation positions.

decide-locally.rationale: Ervin envisions a federation of decentralized communes and community councils holding decisions at the local level, with delegates only coordinating.

rehabilitation.rationale: Ervin says schools and social services, not prisons, answer crime, opposes the death penalty and proposes rehabilitation clinics.

traditional-family.rationale: Anarchist texts here treat the family unit as one site of state loyalty and patriarchy, and Ervin attends to sexual abuse within Black communities; inferred, not directly discussed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Alston's vision includes gay, lesbian, bisexual and transgender Black communities, though anarchists often reject state-sanctioned marriage itself; support is inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Ervin rejects sexism and Alston condemns patriarchal hierarchy, so bodily autonomy for women follows from the tendency's anti-oppression stance.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ervin lists religious dictates among oppressions and says anarchism does not believe in deities, while Alston accepts religious communities; public religious authority is rejected.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Ervin calls for reparations for slavery and later exploitation paid into community cooperatives and credit unions, and treats anti-racism as central.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Alston's inclusion of transgender communities and opposition to patriarchy imply this, but the sources do not discuss gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ervin expects nation-states to be discarded and favors a transnational federation, while Alston values Black cultural pride; preserving a national culture as such is not a priority.

gradual-change.rationale: Ervin calls for revolution, general strikes and dual power and rejects the system's institutions as illegitimate.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Ervin opposes racist harassment and discrimination of undocumented workers and anarchists recognize no national borders.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Ervin views states and their finance-capital bodies as instruments of domination; adherents favor federations from below, not powerful bodies like the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Ervin sees global capital and its institutions as exploiters, and the tendency opposes capitalist markets generally.

nation-first.rationale: Adherents reject national borders and interests of states, favoring internationalist solidarity among oppressed peoples.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Adherents oppose state militaries and imperial wars, though they support armed solidarity from below; state intervention is inferred to be rejected.

open-borders.rationale: Anarchists do not recognize national borders and Ervin opposes discrimination against undocumented workers.

limit-growth.rationale: Sources mention ecology only as an influence on anarchism; adherents are split on degrowth versus redistributing abundance.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Ecology is listed as an influence on anarchist thought but climate policy through government action sits uneasily with anti-statism; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Sources want science and technology made to serve the people but do not credit technology alone with solving problems; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear weapons are condemned and ecology is valued; nuclear power itself is not discussed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Ervin argues for social revolution and accepts any level of violence necessary to enforce the people's demands, within popular support.

experts-over-public.rationale: Ervin demands direct democracy by community councils and rejects rule by vanguards or professionals.

central-planning.rationale: Ervin condemns Stalinist states as authoritarian and favors federations of communes and workers' councils over state direction.

socialized-markets.rationale: Ervin's anarchist communism abolishes wage labor and money in favor of distribution by need, though he notes some anarchists accept exchange among voluntary associations.

land-value-tax.rationale: A state-collected tax-and-keep arrangement is not the adherents' model; they seek common ownership of land; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek to abolish inheritance of wealth along with property but do not rely on state taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional payments from the state do not fit the anti-state, distribution-by-need model, though Ervin demands reparations; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The tendency is internationalist and anti-state, so protecting industry through state tariffs is not favored; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ervin rejects state economic direction, including that of Marxist states, and wants workers' councils to control production.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Ervin prefers common ownership and cooperatives to broad private ownership, though small holders are not the enemy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Ervin states that anarchist communism abolishes the wage system and private and state property, and Parsons-era anarchists likewise attack wage slavery.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Adherents want money abolished but not left to the market; this statement's market clause conflicts with their view so it is neither agreed nor rejected.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized class bodies setting wages contradict the abolition of the state and wage system that Ervin advocates.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ervin states that power to the people does not mean a government or political party ruling in their name and criticizes vanguard parties as authoritarian.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule is a hierarchy the tendency rejects with all government; inferred from anti-statism.

democracy-best.rationale: Ervin favors direct democracy but denounces existing American democracy as phony; adherents accept neither representative democracy nor voters' errors as the standard.

direct-votes.rationale: Ervin favors direct democracy through community councils and assemblies, though by consensus and delegates rather than referendum on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Ervin describes production and community life organized by workers' councils and community councils rather than parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Ervin accepts that Black Americans are a colonized nation with a right to self-determination, and federations of voluntary communes imply a freedom to leave.

natural-rulers.rationale: Ervin rejects permanent leaders and vanguards and Baker's view that strong people do not need strong leaders is cited as formative.

political-violence-never.rationale: Ervin accepts any level of violence necessary and endorses armed defense and insurrection supported by the people.

war-builds-character.rationale: War between states is not glorified; Ervin accepts defensive violence only; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Ervin opposes religious authority and Alston welcomes religious communities as free associations, which implies no state religion; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ervin lists religious dictates among oppressions and opposes government law in general.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Ervin wants defense and justice provided by community councils and militia, and rejects market anarchism; capitalist security firms contradict anti-capitalism.

military-superiority.rationale: Adherents oppose state militaries and imperial rivalry.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Alston builds a diverse Black community including gay, religious and other groups and rejects sexist ethnic nationalism, while valuing Black self-determination; a nation defined by ethnicity is not the aim.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Ervin treats class and race together as drivers of struggle, but Alston warns that struggles are not just against capitalism, so class is not the sole engine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Ervin's distribution by need and reparations point towards material equality; not explicitly stated for outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Black anarchists oppose colonialism and settler domination, so support for Indigenous land authority follows, though the sources focus on Black communities.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Ervin demands reparations for slavery and exploitation and regards African states as puppets of finance capital; reparations for colonized nations are consistent.

civilizational-union.rationale: Ervin anticipates the end of nation-states and favors a transnational federation of Black communities, not unions of states by civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Mutual aid and solidarity are the ethic; Ervin's collective model rejects the egoism of self-interest as the moral guide.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The tendency does not subordinate individuals to the community but stresses voluntary mutual obligation; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ervin lists ecology among movements enriching anarchism, and the sources say humans should coexist with nature.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; coercive population control conflicts with the anti-racist critique of such policies; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed directly; adherents criticize capitalist industry but do not reject industrial society as primitivists do.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology should serve the people, but the sources do not endorse disruption for its own sake; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: None of the Black anarchist sources discuss bodily technology, and adherents plausibly split between autonomy arguments and worries about capitalist access.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by algorithm is government by another name and contradicts direct community democracy.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Panther-era surveillance and police repression make privacy from the state attractive; not directly stated.

restore-past-order.rationale: Ervin seeks revolutionary transformation to a classless stateless society, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents hold firm principles about means and ends and are explicitly ideological; pragmatic outcome-testing is not their guide.

direct-action.rationale: Ervin rejects voting for Black politicians as a path to power and advocates rent strikes, squatting, wildcat and general strikes and direct action against fascists.

means-match-ends.rationale: Ervin builds revolutionary organization from rotating recallable delegates, consensus and federation, mirroring the free society he wants, and Alston says Power to the People not the Party.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Ervin advocates a modern federation of communes with production by workers, not a foraging life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rotating tasks is a practice in organizations, but the sources do not call for abolishing division of labor altogether.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Ervin cites the principle from each according to ability, to each according to need as that of anarchist communism.

production-for-use.rationale: Ervin's anarchist communism aims at production to meet needs rather than profit and criticizes capitalism's commodity production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Ervin holds capitalism is inherently exploitative and racist and creates economic exiles of Black people.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ervin criticizes Marxist-Leninist vanguard rule as authoritarian and compares Stalinist states with fascist police states.

collective-farming.rationale: Ervin's common ownership and communes imply collective land use, but farming is not specifically discussed.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Alston and Ervin link capitalism and finance capital to imperial domination; the inevitability of great power wars is not specifically argued.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and its taxes, but they also seek reparations from it and do not frame taxation as theft in the libertarian sense.

harm-principle.rationale: Anarchists reject state restriction of anything; this statement concedes a limited state, so rejection is mild; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Black anarchists emphasize collective self-determination of the Black community alongside individual freedom, so rights belong to groups too.

conscription.rationale: Ervin calls for volunteer, elected, recallable community defense units and rejects state compulsion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Ervin rejects both state voting and the state itself; community voice through councils is central rather than exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Governments as businesses fuse state and capital, both of which Ervin rejects.

positive-liberty.rationale: Ervin ties freedom to material means: housing, jobs, schools and community institutions funded by reparations.

media-academia-power.rationale: Power is located in the state and capital, not mainly in universities and media; not discussed directly.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Ervin treats racism as built into capitalism and calls reverse racism a myth; racial hierarchy of ability is the ideology of oppressors.

organic-representation.rationale: Ervin favors direct delegates from community councils and workplaces, which resembles trade-body representation, but he rejects parliamentary bodies of any kind.

total-state.rationale: Ervin condemns state domination in all forms and compares Stalinist control to fascist police states.

national-rebirth.rationale: Alston criticizes sexist, authoritarian nationalism like Farrakhan's, and anarchists reject a nation's rebirth through state power.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ervin opposes imperialism and states altogether.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal-style loyalty hierarchy is the opposite of the non-hierarchical federation Ervin proposes.

bound-labor.rationale: Black anarchists descend from the history of slavery and denounce wage labor and coerced work.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Black anarchists criticize Eurocentric white anarchism and draw on Black experience as knowledge, but the sources do not discuss epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; adherents stress both universal liberation and situated Black experience.

single-common-good.rationale: Ervin wants plural communities and consensus federation, with the conflicts of oppressed and oppressors acknowledged rather than one reasoned common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A state of any kind is rejected by anarchists and imperial settler projects are opposed; Israel is not discussed in the sources.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; nations and citizenship are rejected but the right of return is not discussed.

revive-national-language.rationale: State language policy is not an adherent aim; not directly addressed.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Ervin demands rank-and-file democratic control of unions and workers' management of industry through councils.

school-vouchers.rationale: Ervin favors community-run schools, though not by market vouchers; not directly addressed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State fiscal policy is not addressed; adherents seek abolition of the state economy rather than choosing a macro stance.

economic-freedom.rationale: Capitalist economic freedom is rejected as racist exploitation, though freedom from the state is wanted; the claim is therefore mostly disagreed.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rulers of any kind are rejected; Ervin favors rotating, recallable delegates.

national-self-determination.rationale: Ervin says Black Americans are a colonized nation entitled to self-determination, but through free federation, not necessarily in its own state.

force-without-un.rationale: Adherents oppose state militaries and imperial force abroad.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anarchism does not believe in deities but Alston welcomes religious communities; the sources do not say that reason alone must guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Ervin opposes racist harassment of undocumented workers and anarchists do not recognize borders, so benefits should not turn on citizenship.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Ervin demands relief benefits free of racism and sexism and distribution by need, not by work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: Ervin's class struggle outlook rejects partnership with employers and calls for class suicide of white workers' privilege.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favor community-run institutions and radical change but not destruction of libraries.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialism is shared but Ervin criticizes states of the Global South as puppets of finance capital, so a front of states is unlikely favored.

workers-nation.rationale: Ervin favors an international or transnational federation, not nation-bound workers' organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Ervin demands rotating leadership especially to women and says no one can be free while half of society is oppressed.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; adherents abolish money and credit systems, not just interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Ervin's anti-racism targets institutional racism, and segregation law is its core example.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Ervin says government is part of the problem and capitalism and the state operate hand in hand against Black people.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Ecology is respected and capitalist extraction opposed, but the sources do not discuss fossil fuels.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Ervin and Alston defend autonomous cultures and oppose discrimination against undocumented workers.

elite-replacement.rationale: The claim is a racist conspiracy theory opposed to the movement's anti-racism and support for undocumented workers.

proportional-representation.rationale: Ervin rejects voting in state elections, so electoral reform is no concern; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Ervin opposes imperialism and states imposing their system on others.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Alston and Ervin criticize sexism and hierarchy in movements and society and seek to dismantle them.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ervin criticizes Black faces in high places and politicians generally as unfit to deliver liberation.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic restrictions are racist and statist, and conflict with the movement's opposition to the state controlling bodies.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Ervin demands prosecution of killer cops and release of political prisoners.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ervin says the state is unnecessary and part of the problem, and capitalist property protection is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial hierarchy and discouraging mixing contradict Ervin's anti-racism and the movement's ally-building.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anti-racism and the anti-hierarchy ethos imply equal worth, though equal legal rights before state law is not the adherent's frame.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seek international revolution but do not debate this Marxist doctrine.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Ervin argues Black Americans are a colonized nation and criticizes American democracy as a system of domination built on conquest.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Adherents reject state law of any kind, so a uniform code is neither a goal nor a threat; the sources do not discuss religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Alston accepts diverse religious communities; state restriction of belief contradicts anti-statism.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: State bans on practice are rejected; not discussed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Ervin proposes community-run schools and opposes religious dictates, so state religious instruction is rejected.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Ervin criticizes Marxist states as authoritarian and holds that the state must be abolished, not strengthened.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Direct democracy and recallable delegates reflect consent, but adherents go further and reject rule even by consent of a majority.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist state economics is rejected; inferred from anti-capitalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling minorities contradicts the movement's anti-racism and support for undocumented workers.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Ervin accepts any necessary violence for the people's demands but opposes initiating terror without popular support; the statement is mostly rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Cooperation and mutual aid are the model, with competition identified with capitalism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anarchists oppose state bans but Ervin supports direct action against fascists; the state-ban idea is not their method.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anarchists object to arbitrary power as such, and Ervin calls power to the people staying with the people.

separated-powers.rationale: Adherents reject the state itself, so dividing state power is a minor reform at best.

vanguard-party.rationale: Ervin favors catalyst groups rather than vanguard parties and criticizes Leninist vanguard rule as authoritarian.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Ervin's reparations, community institutions and distribution by need prioritize the Black poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Ervin favors tenant-run cooperatives and seizing slum housing, not individual ownership by state-sold sales.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Ervin advocates rent strikes, wildcat and general strikes as central tactics.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Ervin attributes poverty to capitalism and racism, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Alston envisions a plural Black community and Ervin builds multiracial solidarity of anti-racist allies.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rotation and recall are favored, but the sources do not endorse lotteries; offices as such are rejected.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Ervin condemns state repression and police states.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State price fixing is not discussed; adherents want distribution by need but not through state action.

party-controls-media.rationale: Ervin condemns ideological suppression in Stalinist states.

party-commands-army.rationale: Ervin criticizes party-run states; defense units should be elected and recallable and not an occupying force.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Anarchists reject borders and citizenship; Ervin supports undocumented workers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Ervin proposes delegates subject to recall and rotation without privileges, and anarchists call for unpaid or modestly paid delegates, but elected representation itself is not their aim.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Alston contrasts power to the people with power to the party and Ervin warns against parties ruling in the people's name.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions of states are not what federation from below means; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Ervin wants no state head, and defense by elected militia.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hierarchical religious authority is a hierarchy the movement opposes; Alston stresses non-hierarchy.

clerical-rule.rationale: Ervin lists religious dictates among oppressions and opposes all rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Ervin rejects the state's wars and class-collaboration, but the sources do not discuss revolutionary defeatism directly.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ervin demands rotation of roles and no permanent leaders, the opposite of unlimited tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Ervin demands delegates subject to immediate recall and elected defense forces subject to recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Adherents oppose state militaries and alliances but the issue is not discussed.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Ervin supports rent strikes and tenant cooperatives, but universal home ownership is not stated.

people-in-arms.rationale: Ervin calls for a Black peoples' militia self-managed by workers and community and community self-defense units.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Ervin's focus is urban communities; no idealization of rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources criticize the Black petty-bourgeois leadership but not university education as such.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anti-racism rejects hierarchies of civilization, though not explicitly worded; Alston values Black cultural distinctiveness.

death-penalty.rationale: Ervin opposes the death penalty and prisons.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Ervin urges education to end patriarchy and community-run schools, though not by the state; direction supports.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anarchism does not believe in deities, and Ervin calls for educating against oppression; not directly addressed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose state restriction but criticize sexism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Anarchists reject citizenship and borders; descent-based citizenship is an ethnic hierarchy.

minority-language-support.rationale: Self-determination of communities implies this, though not discussed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; adherents reject state law altogether.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Alston's inclusion of varied communities and individuals suggests this, but Mill's argument is not discussed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Ervin treats African states as puppets of European finance capital and wants an end to debt peonage; direct statement on sovereign debt is lacking.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ervin argues that African nation-states often serve as puppets of European finance capital and that Black capitalism does not free people.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Ervin favors community councils from below rather than writing a state constitution; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Ervin condemns authoritarian states that suppress plurality.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Ervin calls for reparations to Black communities, but state aid is not the method; this is mildly supportive.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Adherents oppose state militaries. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The state head is rejected; the question is moot but electing rulers is not endorsed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Ervin's rejection of finance capital and the wage system includes central banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims by states are rejected; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Ervin goes beyond and abolishes private property for common ownership, which is a stronger form of the claim.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Ervin criticizes Soviet-style states as authoritarian police states; the specific state-capitalist label is not used in the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Ecology is an influence on the movement but this principle is not discussed.

collective-defense.rationale: State military pacts are opposed. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Ervin treats Black America as colonized; the statement is consistent with anti-imperialism but not directly discussed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Anarchists oppose religious authority but also state authority, so subordination to the state is not the answer.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Anarchists reject heads of state altogether.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Ervin supports self-determination and federation by voluntary association.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Ervin's federation of communes allows local arrangements, but the sources do not discuss regions inside larger states with special legal systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Anarchism does not believe in deities and rejects rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; flat tax favors the rich, while adherents want redistribution.

character-from-environment.rationale: Ervin attributes the harm in Black communities, including drug use and violence, to oppression and capitalism, not innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Ervin rejects rulers and treats law as an instrument of oppression.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; priorities are social liberation and community needs.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rule by the few and many in a constitution is state structure that adherents reject.

leader-cult.rationale: Ervin and Alston reject leaders and warn against the party-centered cult of leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: The sources do not discuss custody law, and an adherent would prefer community solutions to court presumptions without a stated position.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Ervin warns that Marxist-Leninist parties become a new ruling class, matching this claim.

land-redistribution.rationale: Ervin supports seizing slumlords' housing for tenants and common ownership of land and housing.

refugee-return.rationale: Anti-imperialism and no borders support return, though not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Ervin and Alston reject nation-state expansion and borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Anarchism opposes religious dictates and state punishment.

women-must-cover.rationale: Ervin and Alston oppose patriarchy and state coercion. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

common-currency.rationale: Money is to be abolished and finance capital opposed; a bloc currency is not a goal.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ervin favors a transnational Black federation, an aspect of kinship unity, but anarchists reject unions of states.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Ervin and Alston stress autonomous Black institutions within a federal framework, but anarchists do not accept a state container.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Ervin and Alston organize for liberation in the US rather than emigration, though they see Black America as a colonized nation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Alston says struggles are not just against capitalism and Ervin includes race; the strict materialist claim is not accepted.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anarchists want concentrations abolished through revolution, not state anti-trust.

no-bailouts.rationale: Ervin rejects state support of capitalists but the sources do not address bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rule by national majority is rejected, as Black Americans are a minority; and courts are state institutions.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Ervin rotates leadership especially to women and people of color but rejects formal state bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Colonial blocs and state economic closure are opposed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; binding state agreements are not the adherents' method.

moral-incentives.rationale: Ervin's principle from each according to ability supports non-material motivation, but this is not stated.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Ervin rejects simple terrorism without popular support, favoring mass-based insurrection, though some adherents joined the Black Liberation Army. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anti-hierarchy and abolition of property mean hereditary titles go; Ervin demands equal power to all.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Alston wants anarchism to reflect Black experience, but not a nation-centered school syllabus.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ervin's anti-colonial and anti-racist views reject paternalistic rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ervin condemns phony American democracy and nationalism of states.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Ervin demands an end to racial discrimination in jobs and benefits through reparations and community power.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money is to be abolished and finance capital opposed; state money creation is not the aim.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Ervin sees capitalism as perpetually crisis-ridden, although it survives through co-optation like Black capitalism.

delink-world-market.rationale: Ervin sees African states as puppets of finance capital, yet the sources neither endorse delinking nor integration.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Ervin says white workers must give up privileged status; this resembles the labor aristocracy thesis, but it is not fully endorsed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Ervin treats private and structural discrimination as core oppressions; no property right permits it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Anarchists reject state constitutions as safeguards.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonial stance implies this; not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers are rejected altogether; election is no better.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus decision-making is used but the sources do not specify a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Ervin and Alston endorse resistance to rulers, though anarchists reject rulers entirely.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Ervin states that workers' councils and community councils, not parliaments, hold power.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Ecology and anti-oppression imply some concern but not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The sources mention ecology and coexistence with nature but do not address animal use for food or research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aid should come as mutual aid and reparations, not paternalistic duty of elites.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ervin and Alston call for organizing, community power and struggle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Ervin criticizes the drug economy and media as pacifying, though not explicitly mass culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Alston and Ervin describe cooptation by Black politicians, partly consistent; not an explicit theory.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Ervin says African states act as puppets of European finance capital, implying extraction.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anarchists reject citizenship tests and offices; Ervin supports undocumented workers.

party-own-road.rationale: Anarchists reject parties and Marxist-Leninist ones, but autonomy from foreign parties fits; not discussed.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Ervin emphasizes community self-reliance and cooperatives, though sources do not discuss international development.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anarchists reject political leadership by any group, yet support Indigenous self-determination; the statement's premise of rule by descent conflicts with that.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Ervin advocates direct action against fascist groups but would not found a state constitution.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Ervin compares Stalinist states with fascist police states but also treats racism and capitalism as the main enemy and not equivalent.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Ervin says capitalism was built on slavery and colonial oppression of Africans.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Symbols of racial oppression are rejected; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Patriarchy is treated as structural oppression of women; this equivalence is not made.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Ervin highlights Black women as main victims of sexual violence and abuse.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; Alston urges a distinctly Black anarchism but not civilizational relativism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Ervin opposes state military and calls to demilitarize police; the military is not a guardian.

paid-care-work.rationale: Ervin calls for ending sexism in job opportunities; payment for care work is not discussed.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligation is not discussed; adherents criticize the family as a site of state loyalty but also stress mutual aid.

office-by-exam.rationale: Offices and officials are rejected; rotation and recall are preferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State blocking is not the method; capitalists are opposed regardless of nationality.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Freedom of association and anti-patriarchy suggest this, though not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Ervin states delegates are subject to immediate recall and bound by the community that sent them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private market accounts conflict with common provision by need.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Ervin's common ownership implies use-based holding; usufruct is not named.

single-official-language.rationale: State imposition of language conflicts with community autonomy and anti-assimilation stance.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land is to be held in common, not by nationality; discrimination by nationality is not endorsed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Black anarchism targets structural and institutional racism, not only overt bigotry, per Wikipedia's account of its critique of colorblindness.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Ervin criticizes capitalist commodity production for profit not need.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State arming is opposed, though solidarity with liberation movements is supported.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Ervin opposes imperial domination by states.

corporate-influence.rationale: Ervin says capitalists and politicians control phony American democracy.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: State incentives are not favored; not addressed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local control suits decentralization but exclusion cuts against anti-border stance.

job-guarantee.rationale: Wants abolition of wage labor but also jobs for Black unemployed; state guarantee is not the method.

democratic-peace.rationale: Ervin treats American democracy as phony and imperial.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Ervin rejects government legitimacy and urges rent strikes, squatting and tax resistance.

non-intervention.rationale: Anarchists oppose state interference but support solidarity; the absolute claim is not their view.

industrial-unions.rationale: Ervin's anarcho-syndicalist unions are rank-and-file and industry-wide.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The claim is a racist conspiracy theory and contradicts the movement's anti-racism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Anarchists reject state institutions; marriage specifically is not discussed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not discussed; transparency is consistent with community democracy.

local-production.rationale: Ervin favors community self-provision and cooperatives, and quilombo-like self-sufficient spaces.

informal-organisation.rationale: Ervin favors catalyst groups and federations of local groups, including affinity groups, so partly yes and partly no.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Both state law and international bodies are rejected; no preference.

religious-nation.rationale: Alston envisions plural religious and non-religious Black communities.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Community control supports local retention but not discussed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Ervin's anarchist communism abolishes private property in means of production but not personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Ervin is anti-capitalist and communist in the anarchist sense, and not anticommunist.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ervin says anarchism does not believe in deities, but Alston welcomes Saturday and Sunday religious communities in his vision, and no source predicts religion fading.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Ervin sees capitalism as built on slavery and exile, not as progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ervin ties ending patriarchy to education and ending sexism in jobs and relief and anarchist communism to overall liberation.

socialized-care.rationale: Not addressed; community provision suits, but not discussed.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not discussed; language purism is a nationalist project opposed here.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties between a government and a nation within it are not discussed; adherents distrust states and their treaties yet defend colonized peoples' claims.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ervin describes a stateless, classless, voluntary, cooperative federation of decentralized communes holding resources in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-engineered settlement of minority regions conflicts with anti-racism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ervin's own system is anarchist communism, so he rejects capitalism and Marxist communism but not communism per se.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed; adherents do not rest on historic claims by states.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts anti-racism and anti-fascism; inferred from direct action against fascists.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Alston criticizes homophobia and includes gay, lesbian and transgender communities in his vision.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ervin condemns suppression of ideological plurality by Stalinist states.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Anarchism opposes religious dictates and state punishment.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ervin treats Black Americans as a colonized nation and rejects colonial domination.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; religious obligation is not a basis, though resistance to invasion is supported.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious law as a ground for rule is rejected. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ervin proposes direct democracy through community councils and assemblies and consensus.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Wikipedia describes Black anarchism as examining how multiple systems of domination interact, and Alston rejects reducing struggle to capitalism alone.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Alston's vision explicitly includes transgender communities.

assisted-dying.rationale: The sources do not mention end-of-life care and adherents' views on bodily autonomy versus medical hierarchy are not recorded.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Alston and Ervin are firmly on the revolutionary left and critical of reconciling ideas.

alienated-labor.rationale: Ervin's critique of wage slavery implies alienation; not worded as such.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Contradicts anti-racism and Black communities that include Muslims; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Anarchism does not believe in deities and rejects authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose state coercion in both directions.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ervin rejects capitalism with a welfare face and the state.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Ervin wants state military and police disarmed and replaced by community militia, so state forces abolished but arms kept.

rich-first.rationale: Ervin demands equality, reparations and distribution by need.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anarchists oppose state blocs; not discussed.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary power is a hierarchy rejected. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit unions and cooperatives are favored for reparations money, but money itself is to be abolished.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Ervin treats African states as puppets of European finance capital; refusing is consistent.

property-franchise.rationale: Property-based voting is plutocratic and racist; rejected.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ervin says humans should coexist with nature and opposes patriarchy and domination.

reification.rationale: Not worded; capitalism critique broadly supports.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Ervin says phony democracy is controlled by businesspeople and politicians.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers and law; not a goal.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ervin's anti-racism and rejection of voting both oppose racial exclusion.

online-participation.rationale: Community assemblies and councils are the favored forum, and the sources say nothing about online deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: The tendency seeks to replace government, so open records matter less, and the sources do not discuss it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Alston supports free, diverse communities. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Racist targeting of a minority; Ervin supports boycotts only as economic pressure against oppressors.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random selection not discussed; community assemblies favored but not by sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Alston values religious communities but does not comment on doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ervin connects wealth and capitalist power to domination of Black communities.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Alston supports LGBT inclusion but anarchists oppose the state's military.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: State promotion of anything conflicts with anti-statism; Alston values religious communities.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Ervin writes Abolish prisons and calls for replacing police with community self-defense.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Mutual aid is central but not charity; reparations are demanded as justice.

term-limits.rationale: Rotation applies to delegates; electing politicians is rejected.

vote-delegation.rationale: Recall favored but delegation to experts is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not discussed; adherents prioritize ending racial and class oppression now.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Ervin opposes patriarchy and demands leadership to women.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ervin opposes patriarchy and supports women's equality.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Ervin supports undocumented workers and anarchists reject citizenship barriers.

rent-control.rationale: Ervin supports rent strikes, but state control is not endorsed as end.

abolish-ip.rationale: Abolition of property and commodity production implies this; not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national youth movements are state hierarchies; rejected.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Alston and Ervin oppose state military machinery. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Imperial bases are opposed. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Ervin treats enslavement and colonization as crimes owed reparations.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Ervin abolishes ownership-based profit and uses distribution by need.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Ervin endorses armed self-defense against racist attacks.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Alston stresses Black identity but critiques essentialist nationalism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Alston includes transgender communities but the sources do not take a theoretical position on whether sex is socially constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources stress sexism and women's leadership but do not discuss the category of woman in feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed; Black anarchists honor prisoners and fallen comrades, but not for nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Anarchism does not believe in deities, per Ervin; struggle is material.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Ervin favors a transnational Black federation, but a homeland as cultural centre for a diaspora is not discussed.

culture-before-state.rationale: Alston values cultural pride but seeks no state.

god-not-male.rationale: Alston lists religious communities among those he envisions, without any comment on how God is described.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious interpretation is not discussed, though adherents oppose patriarchy; no stated position.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Racial control of economy opposed. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging administrative regions is a state project; Ervin's federation of communes from below does not address it.

independent-unions.rationale: Ervin says rank-and-file control against parties and states.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Ervin calls socialism without workers' councils authoritarian.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Community control of services favored but not via state.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislatures are rejected. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

municipal-property.rationale: Common ownership via communes close, but federated.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Ervin federations with delegates coordinating and recallable.

family-wage.rationale: Anarchist communism abolishes wage labor, so a family wage is not the demand, yet Ervin wants decent jobs and relief; no stated position.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in the sources, apart from Ervin's anti-dope programs.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and adherents would likely prefer community priorities over state research budgets without taking a position.

person-over-state.rationale: Ervin and Alston reject state domination; yet community comes before.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Alston values religious communities but no claim for politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federation from below, not by revocable grants. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

gm-crops.rationale: Ecology is an influence but the sources do not discuss agricultural biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: Ervin's organizing is urban, but environmental comparison of cities and suburbs is not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Alston and Ervin assert Black autonomy and independent organization.

racial-pride.rationale: Alston credits Black nationalism with pride.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Ervin looks beyond nationalism toward a stateless federation, so a nation defined by language alone is not his organizing idea; inferred from his anti-nationalist stance.

communal-electorates.rationale: Anarchists reject electoral representation altogether, so communal electorates are not a model they would endorse; inferred from the rejection of the state.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Black anarchists oppose the state and its security framing, so a plot against 'my country' is not a theme they would adopt; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the aim of free social services run by communities, which includes education without tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not discussed; a state-levied tax runs against anti-statism, and the tendency prefers direct action and community control; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the aim of a lasting, cooperative society built by communities.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Ervin opposes sexism but within a framework of equality, not a distinct feminine outlook; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Anarchists oppose state militarism, though they endorse community armed self-defense; inferred from anti-militarism.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Anarchists condemn secret deals between states and favor transparent, grassroots organizing; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Not discussed; the tendency opposes both capitalism and state power, so giving the state control over capital is not its model; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Ervin rejects the state's monopoly on force and calls for community self-defense units and a people's militia.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from Ervin's anti-imperialist, anti-state outlook, under which soldiers should not fight states' wars; war resistance is not a documented plank here.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalist currents favour worker organisation and direct action, but the sources stress workers' control over bargaining with employers.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: reformist state top-ups for low pay would be seen as palliatives that leave capitalism and the state in place.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the rejection of state authority, with no wish to bind the state by rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the tendency's anti-imperialism, though it would pursue change through movements rather than through state rule-making.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Ervin calls for abolishing the state and replacing it with federated communes and councils.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Ervin offers a general anarcho-communist outline but stresses self-organised communities; inferred as moderate agreement.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist, anti-commodification stance, which opposes pricing nature as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Alston and Ervin move beyond nationalism and reject the state-centred nation, though they keep Black self-determination.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-capitalist solidarity with debtors, though aid via the state is not their method.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Ervin treats Black Americans as a colonized people within the United States, an internal-colony analysis.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian humanist basis of anti-racist anarchism, with little evidence on redesign.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: state funding conflicts with anti-statism, and mainstream media is seen as serving ruling-class interests.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Ervin and Alston treat religion critically as an institution, yet Black religious communities are valued allies; adherents are split.

farm-price-support.rationale: Anarchists reject a state that guarantees prices or buys crops, though cooperative credit would fit; the sources do not address farming.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the state and its armed forces; the sources never discuss nuclear weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: Ervin rejects vanguard and electoral parties in favour of rank-and-file organizing and a stateless federation of communes.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anarchists oppose patriarchy but also oppose state criminal law and prisons, so adherents are split; FGM is not discussed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the tendency's opposition to sexism and patriarchy, though anarchists reject state-defined property law.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and unrelated to the ideology.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and anti-state positions, which distrust both agencies and courts; harm to the community is central, but the legal route is not.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from opposition to hierarchy and to formal state authority, including traditional rulers.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from its libertarian anti-state outlook; Ervin's economy is ecologically minded but never trades liberty for it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Ervin opposes police, prisons and the criminal-justice system as instruments of racial control, so fixed sentences are rejected.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state coercion and nationalism; compelled language requirements are not discussed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anarcho-syndicalist and communist strands favour voluntary rank-and-file organising and reject state-compelled arrangements, though Ervin does not discuss closed shops directly. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

voter-id.rationale: Black anarchists reject state authority and see ID and citizenship requirements as tools of exclusion and white supremacy; they also reject electoral politics.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Opposes state privileging of any group and hierarchy; religion is not a focus, so this is inferred from anti-hierarchy principles.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Rejects the state and electoral politics as a hierarchy that serves the ruling class, so free elections do not make a government legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: Opposes sexism and moral policing of women, inferred from its anti-patriarchal stance; sexual morality is not discussed directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Opposes state repression and control of communications and the state's use of force against communities, inferred from its anarchist principles.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Seeks to abolish the state and capitalism with community-run services rather than any state cash scheme, a market-style replacement of welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: Opposes sexism and champions equal participation, though it rejects the state and electoral office, adherents agree women hold equal rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Adherents criticise patriarchy but many Black anarchists value Black church and community traditions, so they are split; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Anti-racism is central and adherents hold race to be a social and political construct of oppression, though the sources phrase it politically.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Opposes sexism but rejects state agencies as hierarchy, preferring autonomous community organising for gender equality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Anarchist communists reject private claims to land and resources; Ervin's economic vision is communal and collective ownership, so first-come appropriation is rejected. Inferred from that economic program.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anarchists distrust state-run courts and see Western powers as imperial, so they would doubt tribunals backed by states, though they oppose atrocities; inferred from anti-statism.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The tendency is secular-leaning and critical of organized religion's hierarchy, though it respects religious communities; a literal inerrancy claim is not part of it.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Ervin and Alston oppose sexism and homophobia inside nationalist movements, so any self-government must guarantee gender equality from the start.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and bureaucratic rule, and criticize Marxist-Leninist states as new ruling classes; a bureaucratic planned state is not worth defending.

indirect-election.rationale: Federations of local councils with recallable delegates are the anarchist model, which matches delegate selection by lower councils; inferred from anti-leadership federalism.

national-church-status.rationale: Anarchism opposes the state and hierarchy, so a privileged state church is rejected; inferred from this core opposition.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Black self-determination and community control support autonomy for minority-majority regions, though anarchists prefer stateless federation to autonomy within a state; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Anarchists favour self-determination by communities but reject the state frame of choosing which country a territory joins; adherents would be split and the issue is unaddressed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anarchists reject state borders as arbitrary and imposed, so they would not defend colonial borders as such; inferred from anti-statism and anti-colonialism.

simple-living.rationale: Communal self-reliance appeals but the tendency focuses on social revolution, not austerity; the sources do not address it and adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Self-determination and anti-colonial views favour protecting indigenous homelands against outside settlement, though anarchists dislike state restrictions; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Anarchists oppose conscription and the military draft as state coercion, which argues for neither rather than equal draft; inferred, partial fit with the 'or neither' clause.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Black anarchists reject nation-state patriotism and duty to defend the national territory, favouring community self-determination; inferred from their anti-state stance.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: They oppose state violence and policing, especially its racial targeting of Black communities, and would reject killing without trial; inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: They oppose all state powers and capitalist great-power blocs, so alignment with the Chinese state is unattractive; inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: A state acting for its nation abroad runs against their rejection of states and nations as political units; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Anarchist communism holds land and resources in common, but the compensation framing is a Georgist idea they do not use; inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: Opposition to slavery and coercion makes bodily autonomy central, though they reject the property-based framing; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Regressive taxes hit poor communities hardest, but they reject the state and its tax system altogether; inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: They favour mutual aid and universal communal provision over state means-testing; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: They reject leaders and the state; rank-and-file organising and Ella Baker-style anti-leadership politics oppose a leader-centred model; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: They oppose capitalism and state favours to corporations, though they want business abolished rather than merely un-privileged; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Anarchists oppose religious authority in politics and organise across lines; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; Afrocentric currents value ancestral heritage but the tendency has no unified view; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: They oppose sexism and patriarchy, including within Black nationalist movements, so women's right to leave a marriage is accepted; inferred from that opposition.

national-resource-control.rationale: They oppose state ownership; resources should be held by communities, not by a national government; inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Ervin treats existing wealth as built on slavery and exploitation, so process alone does not justify it; the sources do not state a theory of distribution.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Anarchists reject state taxation and institutions, so they would not endorse a state-imposed tax; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Ervin presents racism as a continuing central force that Black liberation must confront alongside capitalism and the state.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Anarchists deny the state's legitimacy and favour direct action against unjust laws; the natural-law wording is inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Its anarcho-communist aims of abolishing wage labour fit automation to reduce work; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Its decentralist, federated vision opposes concentrated power, which suits a plural world; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Its anarcho-communist and syndicalist strand draws on the classical socialist view that workers create value; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Alston's essay argues for going beyond nationalism, and Ervin rejects nationalism that seeks state power, so love of country as a political bond is rejected.

material-over-identity.rationale: Ervin insists that race and class struggle go together and criticises class-only politics, so identity issues are not to be sidelined.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Ervin rejects vanguard parties, the state and capitalism together, so a party-led market socialism is opposed.

missingStatements.text: Black Americans are a colonized people with a right to self-determination.
missingStatements.rationale: Ervin argues that Black Americans are a colonized nation and that self-determination includes an independent Black movement.

missingStatements.text: Armed self-defense by communities against racist attacks is justified.
missingStatements.rationale: Ervin endorses armed community self-defense units and a Black peoples' militia, and the Wikipedia account lists armed self-defense among the tendency's practices.

missingStatements.text: Radical movements should be organized without permanent leaders, through federations of local groups with rotating, recallable delegates.
missingStatements.rationale: Ervin proposes federations with rotating duties and immediately recallable delegates, and Alston cites Ella Baker against leadership-led revolution.

notes: Contested points include how far Black nationalism should be embraced (Ervin accepts it as a basis for autonomy, Alston wants it stripped of sexism and hierarchy), armed struggle versus nonviolent tactics, and the Panther-derived emphasis on survival programs. Most answers not stated by the sources are inferences from anti-statism and anti-racism and are marked accordingly.
